title: Minimum and maximum values of a function
competency: Find absolute extrema on closed intervals and relative extrema by the first derivative test.

keywords.def: The largest value of f on its whole domain or interval.
A value f(c) bigger than every nearby value of f.
Using the sign change of f′ at a critical number to find maxima and minima.
A number c in the domain where f′(c) = 0 or f′(c) does not exist.

ideas.name: Absolute maximum and minimum on [a, b]

en.text: On a closed interval the largest and smallest values happen at a critical number or at an endpoint. So: find the critical numbers inside [a, b], work out f there and at a and b, then pick the largest and smallest.

am.text: በዝግ ክፍተት [a, b] ላይ ትልቁና ትንሹ እሴት በወሳኝ ቁጥር ወይም በጫፍ ላይ ይገኛሉ።

screens.title: Where is the top?
screens.ask: f(x) = x² − 2x on [−1, 2]. Where is f largest?
screens.after:
Work out f at the candidates.
f(−1) = 1 + 2 = 3. f(0) = 0. f(1) = 1 − 2 = −1. f(2) = 4 − 4 = 0.
The largest value, 3, is at the endpoint x = −1.
x = 1 is the bottom of the valley, the minimum.

screens.title: Relative and absolute extrema
paras: f(c) is a relative (local) maximum if f(c) is bigger than f(x) for all other x near c.
It is an absolute maximum if f(x) ≤ f(c) for every x in the domain.

screens.title: Procedure on [a, b]
paras: Step 1: find all critical numbers of f.
Step 2: evaluate f at the critical numbers in [a, b] and at a and b.
Step 3: the largest is the maximum, the smallest is the minimum.

screens.title: Candidates for f(x) = x² − 2x on [−1, 2]
screens.ask: Tap each candidate: the two endpoints and the critical number.

points.name: a
points.info: Endpoint: f(−1) = 3. The largest: absolute maximum.

points.name: c
points.info: Critical number (f′(1) = 0): f(1) = −1. The smallest: absolute minimum.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The largest value of f on its whole domain or interval.
A value f(c) bigger than every nearby value of f.

screens.text: Find the absolute maximum and minimum values of f(x) = x² + 2x + 3 on [−2, 2] (tap both):
True or false: on a closed interval, the absolute maximum is always where f′ = 0.
screens.why:
The maximum can be at an endpoint, where f′ need not be 0.
Example: x² − 2x on [−1, 2] has its maximum f(−1) = 3 at an endpoint.
There f′(−1) = −4, not 0.
So the statement is false: always check the endpoints.

screens.title: Put the closed-interval method in order
items: Solve f′(x) = 0 and find where f′ does not exist
Keep only critical numbers inside [a, b]
Evaluate f at those and at a and b
Pick the largest and the smallest
screens.why:
Start with the derivative.
Its zeros (and undefined points) are the critical numbers.
Throw away any outside [a, b].
Then compare f at the critical numbers AND both endpoints.
Largest = absolute max, smallest = absolute min.
screens.clue: You cannot find critical numbers before you have f′.

screens.ask: Find the absolute maximum value of f(x) = (x² − 2x + 4)/(x − 2) on [−3, 1]: ___
screens.why:
Quotient rule: f′ = ((2x − 2)(x − 2) − (x² − 2x + 4))/(x − 2)² = x(x − 4)/(x − 2)².
Critical numbers 0 and 4. Only 0 is in [−3, 1].
f(−3) = 19/(−5) = −19/5. f(0) = 4/(−2) = −2. f(1) = 3/(−1) = −3.
The largest is −2.
Trap: −3 > −19/5, but −2 is larger still.
screens.clue: Use the quotient rule; keep only critical numbers in the interval.

screens.ask: Find the absolute maximum value of f(x) = 12x − x³ on [0, 3]: ___

en.text: At a critical number c look at the sign of f′ on each side. − to + means a relative minimum; + to − means a relative maximum; no change means neither. The value is f(c); the place is x = c.

am.text: በወሳኝ ቁጥር c ዙሪያ የ f′ ምልክትን እንመለከታለን፤ ከ − ወደ + ዝቅተኛ፣ ከ + ወደ − ከፍተኛ።

screens.title: Valley or hill?
screens.ask: f′ is negative just left of c and positive just right of c. At c the graph has
screens.after:
f′ < 0 on the left: the graph falls into c.
f′ > 0 on the right: the graph rises out of c.
Falling then rising makes a valley: a relative minimum.

screens.title: First derivative test
paras: If f′ changes from − to + at c, f has a relative minimum at c.
If f′ changes from + to − at c, f has a relative maximum at c.
If the sign does not change, there is no extremum at c.

screens.title: Read the sign change at c
screens.ask: Tap each pattern of f′ around a critical number c.
items: Falls, then rises: a valley. Relative minimum.
Rises, then falls: a hill. Relative maximum.
Rises on both sides (like x³ at 0): no extremum.
Falls on both sides: no extremum.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Using the sign change of f′ at a critical number to find maxima and minima.

screens.title: f(x) = 2x³ + 3x² − 12x − 3
steps: At −2: + to −, a relative maximum f(−2) = 17.
At 1: − to +, a relative minimum f(1) = −10.

screens.title: Hill and valley: y = x³ − 3x²
screens.ask: f′(x) = 3x(x − 2). Tap the dots around each critical number.

points.name: max
points.info: f′ goes + to − at 0: relative maximum f(0) = 0.

points.name: min
points.info: f′ goes − to + at 2: relative minimum f(2) = −4.

screens.text: Use the first derivative test: f(x) = (x − 1)²(x − 3)². At x = 2 there is
screens.why:
f′ = 2(x − 1)(x − 3)² + 2(x − 1)²(x − 3) = 4(x − 1)(x − 2)(x − 3).
Just left of 2 (x = 1.5): f′ > 0. Just right (x = 2.5): f′ < 0.
+ to −: a relative maximum.
Value: f(2) = (1)²(−1)² = 1.
Trap: 0 is the minimum value, at x = 1 and x = 3.
screens.clue: Sign of f′ just before and after 2.

screens.text: Find the relative maximum and minimum values of f(x) = 2x³ − 9x² − 24 (tap both):
screens.why:
f′(x) = 6x² − 18x = 6x(x − 3). Critical numbers 0 and 3.
Signs: + before 0, − between, + after 3.
At 0, + to −: maximum f(0) = −24.
At 3, − to +: minimum f(3) = 54 − 81 − 24 = −51.

screens.text: Find the relative maximum and minimum values of f(x) = (1/4)x³ − 3x (tap both):
screens.why:
f′(x) = (3/4)x² − 3 = (3/4)(x − 2)(x + 2).
Signs: + before −2, − between, + after 2.
Maximum at −2: f(−2) = −2 + 6 = 4.
Minimum at 2: f(2) = 2 − 6 = −4.

screens.text: True or false: f(x) = x³ has a relative minimum at x = 0.
screens.why:
f′(x) = 3x², so 0 is a critical number.
But 3x² > 0 on both sides of 0.
f′ does not change sign, so there is no extremum.
The graph only flattens at 0. False.

screens.title: f(x) = ax³ + bx − 5 has a relative minimum −6 at x = 1/2

screens.ask: Find the unknown constant: f(x) = x³ + ax + b has a relative minimum 4 at x = 2. b = ___
screens.why:
At a relative minimum, f′(2) = 0.
f′(x) = 3x² + a, so 12 + a = 0 and a = −12.
The value is 4: f(2) = 8 + 2a + b = 8 − 24 + b = 4.
b = 20.
Check: f′ = 3(x² − 4) goes − to + at 2, so it is a minimum. ✓

items.text: Find the absolute max and min values of f(x) = x² + 2x + 3 on [−2, 2] (tap both):
items.why:
Critical number: 2x + 2 = 0, x = −1.
f(−2) = 3, f(−1) = 2, f(2) = 11.
Max 11, min 2.

items.text: Find the absolute max and min values of f(x) = x³ + 3x² − 9x + 5 on [−2, 2] (tap both):
Find the absolute max and min values of f(x) = 3x⁴ − 26x³ − 60x² − 11 on [1, 5] (tap both):
items.why:
f′ = 12x³ − 78x² − 120x = 6x(2x² − 13x − 20).
Its zeros are 0, about −1.28 and about 7.78: none in [1, 5].
So only the endpoints count.
f(1) = 3 − 26 − 60 − 11 = −94.
f(5) = 1875 − 3250 − 1500 − 11 = −2886. Max −94, min −2886.

items.text: Find the absolute max and min values of f(x) = (x² − 2x + 4)/(x − 2) on [−3, 1] (tap both):
Find the relative extreme values of f(x) = 2x³ − 9x² − 24 (tap both):
Find the relative extreme values of f(x) = (1/4)x³ − 3x (tap both):
Find the relative extreme values of f(x) = (x² + x + 1)/(x² − x + 1) (tap both):
items.why:
Quotient rule: top of f′ = (2x + 1)(x² − x + 1) − (x² + x + 1)(2x − 1) = −2x² + 2.
f′ = −2(x² − 1)/(x² − x + 1)²: zero at x = ±1.
At −1: − to +, minimum f(−1) = 1/3.
At 1: + to −, maximum f(1) = 3/1 = 3.

items.ask: Find the unknown constant: x³ + ax + b has a relative minimum 4 at x = 2. a = ___
items.why:
At the minimum, f′(2) = 0.
f′(x) = 3x² + a, so 3(4) + a = 0.
a = −12.

test.text: Find the absolute max and min values of f(x) = x² − 4x on [0, 5] (tap both):
First derivative test: f′ goes from + to − at c. Then f(c) is
test.why:
+ before c: the graph rises to c.
− after c: the graph falls away.
Rising then falling makes a hill: a relative maximum.

test.ask: Find the relative minimum value of f(x) = x² − 6x + 1: ___
test.why:
f′ = 2x − 6 = 0 at x = 3.
f′ goes − to + at 3: a minimum.
f(3) = 9 − 18 + 1 = −8.

test.ask: Find the absolute maximum value of f(x) = −x² + 4x on [0, 3]: ___
Find the relative maximum value of f(x) = x³ − 3x: ___

notes.text: Example 1 b (p.107) ends "0 is a relative maximum value and 1 is a relative minimum value"; it should be the reverse (max 1 at x = 2, min 0 at x = 1 and 3).
Note p.103 "At either local maximum or local minimum point the gradient is zero" holds only where f is differentiable (|x| has a minimum at 0 with no derivative).
Exercise 2.15 c: as printed, no critical number lies in [1, 5]; the answer uses the endpoints. Please confirm the printed function.

screens.text: Use the sign of f′: f′(x) = x − 5. Where is f decreasing?
screens.why:
f is decreasing where f′(x) ≤ 0.
x − 5 ≤ 0 gives x ≤ 5.
Check x = 0: f′(0) = −5 < 0. ✓
